data.source_text_main_point: Police raids and voluntary closures across Europe are dismantling major BitTorrent and ed2k link sites, proving that hosting such sites is illegal and exposing operators to prosecution, despite their claims of legal loopholes.

statements.key_statement: European police raids and voluntary closures prove hosting P2P link sites is illegal.
statements.long_statement: Across several European nations, including France, the Netherlands, Finland, and Slovenia, law enforcement raids and voluntary operator decisions have recently shut down major BitTorrent and ed2k link sites. These actions demonstrate that hosting such sites is illegal, effectively dismantling the infrastructure despite the operators' previous arguments regarding legal loopholes.

statements.key_statement: The owner of SuprNova.org voluntarily closed the site following legal warnings.
statements.long_statement: Sloncek, who is 18 years old and runs the Slovenian website SuprNova.org, chose to turn off the site's links section. This decision came after he got legal notices and saw that administrators from other major peer-to-peer networks had been arrested.

statements.key_statement: The SuprNova.org operator voluntarily closed the site following peer-to-peer admin arrests and legal warnings.
statements.long_statement: The operator of the Slovenian-based SuprNova.org link site decided to voluntarily shut down the site's file-sharing section after learning that administrators of other prominent peer-to-peer networks had been arrested and after receiving formal legal warnings from copyright enforcement groups.

statements.key_statement: The SuprNova.org operator plans to stop hosting BitTorrent links while keeping forums online.
statements.long_statement: The operator of the Slovenian-based SuprNova.org link site asserts that the platform will cease distributing BitTorrent files, even though the site's discussion forums and IRC chat network will continue to remain accessible to users.

statements.key_statement: FinReactor, a website based in Finland, has shut down. The MPAA says it is responsible for this closure.
statements.long_statement: The Motion Picture Association of America, a trade association representing major American movie studios, has publicly claimed responsibility for the decision by Finnish authorities to raid and shut down the FinReactor link site, although Finnish investigators have officially denied any direct contact or involvement from the American group.

statements.key_statement: BitTorrent accelerates file distribution by enabling users to exchange file segments rather than relying on a single centralized server.
statements.long_statement: The BitTorrent system, developed by programmer Bram Cohen and introduced in 2002, accelerates file distribution by allowing users to exchange specific file segments with one another instead of downloading entire files from a single centralized server. This decentralized architecture is particularly effective for rapidly spreading new releases to large numbers of people, offering a distinct advantage over traditional peer-to-peer networks that rely on individual users for long-term file availability.
